title: Wagertech <> Jumpr: Referral and Payouts Discovery

items.topic: Build coverage during Kobi's vacation
items.statement: Emily asked for confirmation that another Jumpr resource can fully cover while Kobi is on vacation. Kobi confirmed: his goal is to finish all discovery and designs first so that Wy, Taryn and Cedric can continue the build.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Just to confirm though, Kobe, just in terms of lead and his engagement, kind of like with your vacation, um he'll be able to kind of step in like you'll be able to have him completely step in and kind of cover off where anything you've you're leaving off with. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct. Yeah. My goal is like make sure everything's like designed and scoped out for the team and it I'm hoping it's just a matter of like powering through the build. So between uh Wy Taran and Cedric, they should be able to go through.
items.asr_note: Kobe = Kobi; 'Wy Taran' = Wy, Taryn [ASR?]; 'lead' may be a person's name [ASR?]

items.topic: Referral/payouts least defined work block
items.statement: Joyce said referral and payouts is the least progressed of the big work blocks in terms of pre-existing scope and definition, so the session is a brainstorm rather than a set of firm requirements.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: It's probably like the least progressed out of all our big out of all of our big blocks of work. So, um I'm hoping to make this conversation into more of like a brainstorm versus like me telling you exactly what the requirements are.

items.topic: Batch referrer payments into payout record
items.statement: WagerTech needs a workflow so referrers can be paid across multiple signups: the BA collects signups together and converts them into a separate payout record.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: we need a way of um ensuring that like refer referers um can get uh paid across multiple signups and it's kind of up to the BA to um collect signups together and then convert that into what I would assume is a separate record type of um payout.

items.topic: Dashboard of all cash flow and payouts
items.statement: Joyce stated the ultimate goal is a dashboard tracking all cash flow in and out of the business. From a reporting view this includes referral payments plus money sent to players (first-time deposit and redeposit), BA commissions and redeposit incentives (including personal).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: in my mind, the ultimate goal of this is like, let's have a dashboard that kind of like tracks all of our like cash flow that's going in and out of the business. / Joyce Kiddell: But like from a reporting perspective, we probably want to see like all payouts together and that would be inclusive of what we send players for like deposit like first time deposit and redeposit money. um as well as like the commissions are sending VAS, right? / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. And like obviously my like I'm like including redeposit incentive as like everything including personal.

items.topic: Only referral payments need dedicated workflow
items.statement: Only primary and secondary referral payments need a separate work stream (screens in Salesforce). Other payout types are for reporting only.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, I was just looking at this chart here real quick. Yeah, I mean, we only have primary and secondary referral payments, so / Joyce Kiddell: But yeah, so I agree that those are the only ones that require kind of a separate like work stream like probably like screens in Salesforce.

items.topic: Commission calculation stays outside Salesforce
items.statement: For the launch, Salesforce provides the data and commission calculations stay outside Salesforce in Jay's existing tool. Lina agreed because of the hard November 1 date and because WagerTech already has an internal system; in-Salesforce commission rules can come later.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Is the intention that like all of these are calculated within Salesforce or Salesforce provides the the data to calculate these outside of Salesforce? / Emily Vandenberg: So Lena, the way I would kind of see that is like an integration with um Jay's tool where now just like the data would be coming from like kind of Salesforce and then his tool still kind of doing the the magic in like the first phase. / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, let's set it up that way because we do have a lot of nuances there. / Lina Ceniccola: So I would rather spend less time configuring everything / Lina Ceniccola: on that because it's we have a system for it internally anyway. So that can be a later thing.

items.feature_area: Other (integration of Salesforce data with Jay's commission tool)
items.topic: How Salesforce data reaches Jay's tool
items.statement: Emily described the commission approach as an 'integration' with Jay's tool, but the mechanism (integration vs report/export) was not defined in this meeting.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: So Lena, the way I would kind of see that is like an integration with um Jay's tool where now just like the data would be coming from like kind of Salesforce

items.topic: November 1 is a hard date
items.statement: Lina stated the November 1 date is a pretty hard date.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: think we can handle it internally just because like the this November 1 date is a pretty hard date.

items.topic: Rippling integration for BA commissions later
items.statement: Joyce flagged, as not a right-away item, the move to Rippling for BA commission pay. Lina said an Excel file to upload amounts to Rippling is fine. Kobi has not used Rippling and would have to look into an out-of-the-box integration. Joyce suggested taking the integration discussion offline.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and something to flag that I don't think is a right away thing, but as we're moving towards RIP Lane, which from my understanding is going to handle pay, is that right? / Lina Ceniccola: just on yeah the VA commissions. So say if we get like if we get an Excel file that we can use to upload the amounts to Ripling that's fine. / Kobi Kunasekaran: No, I haven't used playing. I'd have to look into it.
items.asr_note: RIP Lane / Ripling / playing = Rippling; VA = BA [ASR]

items.topic: Discuss integration path offline
items.statement: Joyce suggested talking offline about the integration path, because going to Rippling directly might be faster. No owner or date was stated.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Okay, let me sec cuz Uh yeah, we could just end up using that like after and maybe we like I don't know let's talk about offline in terms of the integration phase tool because it might be faster to go to rippling

items.topic: Release focus: referrer payout batching
items.statement: For this release, the build focuses on the referrer payout batching process, plus the reporting to support it (Emily).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: directly but okay so for the purpose of what we need to build as part of this release um do we want to just focus on the refer payout batching process Emily? / Emily Vandenberg: I think so. And then yeah, just like the reporting to support like the yeah

items.topic: Write-off and clawback for paid fraud signups
items.statement: Emily raised that write-offs need support: when a signup is later found fraudulent after referral payment, it must move into a write-off category / clawback. She said a process is needed but they can start by collecting the data in Salesforce. Lina handles write-offs and said the referral payment is included in the erosion only if it was made, so the signup must show whether the referral payment was paid.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: So being able to, you know, like typically we kind of handle some of that write off within the payment um processing portion, Lena, to be able to like put it back and like actually write off signoffs in Salesforce. I feel like we should solve for that and we'll have to have a process that kind of supports it. But at least we can start um with that data like collecting that data through the system. / Lina Ceniccola: There'd have to be something to point to that like that the referral payment was also paid out for that sign up specifically.

items.topic: Signup shows referral paid / not paid
items.statement: Each signup needs an indication of whether its referral payment was paid. Kobi later confirmed the signup record will be marked as paid for the referral payout via the payout record.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Like in my mind, every sign up should have like some indication if it was the referral payment was paid out or not.

items.topic: Running tally of amount owed to referrer
items.statement: Lina said a running tally that automatically calculates how much a referrer is owed would help the BA. Joyce moved to the flow discussion; no explicit confirmation.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: But from like what would help the brand ambassador is that they have kind of a running tally that automatically calculates like how much that person is owed. / Joyce Kiddell: Let's let's get into the the flow discussion and then I think that'll be covered as part of it.

items.topic: Current build: payout type chosen on signup
items.statement: Kobi's understanding of the current build: the BA chooses the payout type on the signup and the amount populates automatically; he does not recall building anything that pulls from the referrer.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh from my understanding they have to choose the payout type and the amount gets populated onto the signup automatically. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But I don't recall building anything that pulls information from the referral that's added.

items.topic: Kobi to verify default payout type pull
items.statement: Kobi will go back through his notes to confirm whether anything already pulls the default from the referrer; if not, it can be built assuming the right fields exist on the referrer.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, so if that's needed, like would I I'll go back through my notes and confirm if that was like if there's something already there. If not, we should be able to build that out assuming, you know, we have the right fields on the referral

items.topic: Signup payout type defaults from referrer
items.statement: When a BA logs a signup and selects or creates a referrer, the signup payout type defaults from the referrer's default payout type; the BA can change it (cash or bet credit) per signup. For a new referrer the type is chosen at that time.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, but we would want the BA to have the ability to change it if for like that sign up for whatever reason. / Kobi Kunasekaran: when they Sorry, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I just wanted to like read that back. So when uh when a PA goes in to log a signup um and they select a referral or create a referral um the payout type or the signup should pull from the default payout type that's on the referral. Um and but they should be able to change that um to like bet credit or cash um if if they don't want to go with the default. / Joyce Kiddell: Yes, if they're an existing refer obviously, / Joyce Kiddell: but if they're not then you have to fight at that time.

items.topic: Keep the term 'bet credit'
items.statement: WagerTech keeps calling the referral payment type 'bet credit' even though it is technically a redeposit.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: like are are we still clinging at credit because it's like technically a redeposit. / Lina Ceniccola: We do internally. We call it bad credit for referral payments. / Joyce Kiddell: Just keep it like that. / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, I say keep it consistent.
items.asr_note: 'clinging at credit' / 'bad credit' = calling it bet credit / bet credit [ASR]

items.topic: Referrer record shows its primary signups
items.statement: From the referrer record, users can see the signups where that referrer is the primary referrer.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, when you mean like see it They would be able to see the signups where they are the primary / Joyce Kiddell: associated sign. / Kobi Kunasekaran: referral. Yes.

items.topic: Cash payouts: batch or one-to-one
items.statement: Reps typically batch cash referral payments but must also be able to pay a single signup one-to-one.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: They can do onetoone, right, Lena? If it's like an odd, like it's not that they couldn't, but they typically batch / Lina Ceniccola: they strategically they prefer to badge. Work-wise, they prefer to badge. But if someone does one sign up and they're like, I want referral payment, they could do it.

items.topic: Mixed payout types per referrer allowed
items.statement: A referrer can have some signups paid as cash and others as bet credit (rare, about 1%), and the design must leave that open.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Is it possible for a player to have one sign up as cash and one as bad credit? / Lina Ceniccola: Yes. / Lina Ceniccola: allocates half of them as cash half of them as bet credit. It's probably like 1% of people, but leave it open.

items.topic: No mixing cash and bet credit in payout
items.statement: A single payout record cannot combine cash and bet credit; mixed referrers need two separate payout records. Only one payout type can be batched together.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: but I I wouldn't like within a single payout record if we are creating a separate record type or object type whatever it's called. Um I would not combine cash and redeposit into one, right? / Lina Ceniccola: You would have to then create like two different payout records. / Lina Ceniccola: you can only batch one of the same kind of touch.

items.topic: Referrer-level select-and-batch payout screen
items.statement: Joyce described a screen at the referrer level where the rep sees all signups for that referrer, selects (for example) the cash ones and clicks a button to batch payout, which creates a separate payout record. Kobi later read back the same flow (select unpaid signups on the referrer, click create payout) and will design it.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yeah. Makes sense. Um so then once they like this is what I'm envisioning. And let me know if you guys are aligned, but some sort of screen where the rep can go into like a referral level, see all of the signups against that referral and be like, I'm going to select, you know, all the cash ones like 1 2 3 4 and then there's some sort of button that that allows them to batch payout and then it creates a separate record where all of those are collapsed into one / Kobi Kunasekaran: they they pick a bunch uh click like create payout or something like that and that creates a payout record that links back to all of the signups um and aggregates the payout amount based on what the payout amount was in each of those uh signup records.

items.topic: Cash payout tracks date sent
items.statement: For cash payouts the only tracking needed is the date sent (plus the BMO ID, see next item). Reps track this in a spreadsheet today.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Cash payouts just that it was sent / Lina Ceniccola: Yes. / Joyce Kiddell: Um, so yeah, date sent and the BMO ID. That's it.

items.topic: BMO transaction ID field, no screenshot
items.statement: Add a field for the BMO transaction ID on the cash payout so WagerTech can refer back to BMO for auditing. Lina does not want another screenshot proof. Kobi suggested just having the field there.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: like what if they put in ID or something just so you can quickly refer to Beimo for auditing purposes. / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, we can add that field for sure. / Lina Ceniccola: I just want to avoid another screenshot. / Lina Ceniccola: The I the ID is good. / Kobi Kunasekaran: can leave it off show. Just have the field there and then if it makes sense, you can add it later.
items.asr_note: Beimo = BMO; 'leave it off show' unclear, possibly 'leave it optional' or 'leave proof off' [ASR?]

items.topic: Primary and secondary payouts kept separate
items.statement: Payouts cannot combine primary and secondary referral signups: one payout per payout type per referral type. Kobi said to keep them separate at least initially and layer in combination later if needed.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Um, sorry. In terms of batching, did we say this? Like you can only batch like your primary, you can't cross like secondary and primary referral. / Kobi Kunasekaran: is that one one payout per payout type per uh I guess referral type like primary versus secondary. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, it might be better to keep it separate at least for the initial layers and then if we do need a additional combination, maybe we can layer that in afterwards.

items.topic: No e-transfer email field on payout
items.statement: No e-transfer email field is needed on the payout; assume the email is on file for the player.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, do we need to like add a field for e transfer email or do we assume that we already have that on file for the player or refer refer? / Lina Ceniccola: Assume it's on file for player.

items.topic: Payout amount aggregated from signups
items.statement: The payout amount is the sum of the payout amounts on the signups rolled into the payout.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and the the amount would be aggregated based on the payout amounts from the signups that are being rolled up into this payout transaction. / Joyce Kiddell: Yep. But there's there's a matrix,

items.topic: Primary referral amounts from payment matrix
items.statement: Primary referral payout amounts come from a matrix (in the documentation; Kobi has it) based on the referrer's payout type and currency. The matrix sets the payout amount and currency on each signup (e.g. $50 USD).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: right? Like um so if you're attached to something as a prim primary referral um then we have like a grid that's in the documentation somewhere where it's like per refer that you do you get X dollars. / Lina Ceniccola: yes, I Kobihas it. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And that's where the matrix comes in that determines the actual payout based on the referers payout type and the referer's currency.

items.topic: Payout record is single currency
items.statement: A payout record holds one currency. A referrer with signups in CAD and USD needs separate payout records; CAD and USD signups cannot be grouped into one payout.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. If if they do need to get paid out in different currencies, is it okay if those those are going to be like two separate payout records? So the payout record itself is going to be like one currency. / Kobi Kunasekaran: You can't group uh US and Canada into a single payout. / Joyce Kiddell: I think that makes sense. What about you guys? / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, I think so.

items.topic: Referrer default currency, override per signup
items.statement: Each referrer gets a default currency on creation. The BA can override the referral payout currency at the signup level, similar to payout type, to leave room for ad hoc cases (e.g. dual citizen).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, Kobi,maybe it's one of those fields that the BA can customize at a signup level if they want, similar to payment type. Um, but it's inherited from the record as like the default. / Emily Vandenberg: It's like we assign a currency for the refer right upon creation and that's / Emily Vandenberg: the default and with the ability to override right Kobi. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, but the the way the flows it looks like it's going to work though is you have your signup that comes in.

items.topic: Payout currency from selected signups
items.statement: The payout record currency comes from the payout currency on the selected signups (not directly from the referrer). The selection screen segregates signups by currency and blocks choosing multiple currencies. Two currencies exist per signup: the player's and the referrer's.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: They won't be able to choose multiple currency. We would block that out entirely. So depending on what type of signups they se they they select in terms of what the payout currency on the signup is would be the payout currency on the sorry on the payout record itself. / Joyce Kiddell: No, it's confusing because we were like talking in terms of currency per sign up, but like there's really two currencies and there's two amounts.

items.topic: Kobi to diagram currency payout flow
items.statement: Emily found the currency explanation confusing; Kobi said he will draw it out.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: What do you think? I It's kind of confusing and I'm like wondering if / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'll I'll I'll draw it out. I'll draw it out.

items.topic: Paid status closes signups, no double pay
items.statement: The payout record needs a status to show it has been paid. The rep marks it paid/complete with a button, which automatically updates the linked signups as paid and removes them from the payment queue so they are not paid twice.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we'll need some sort of status on the payout record as well to indicate that it's been paid. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So that would be the trigger to go back to the signup records and to mark that they've already been paid out. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yeah. Good call. / Joyce Kiddell: like he they have to come in and hit a button to say complete which then automatically updates the signups and takes them out of the payment queue. / Joyce Kiddell: we definitely can't double pay or triple pay stuff.

items.topic: Phase 1: report amount and mark paid
items.statement: For Phase 1 scoping, Salesforce calculates and shows the payout amount and lets the rep mark it complete; the rep handles the actual payment outside Salesforce.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I'm just thinking through like what we said from like a payout like Salesforce just being able to kind of like report and then obviously mark as paid here. So just like for scoping of phase one, right? / Emily Vandenberg: they take it from there. They they handle it and they and then it just marks as complete. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah.

items.topic: Bet credit payout split by operator
items.statement: For bet credit, after batching (e.g. $500) the rep breaks the amount into smaller deposit amounts across the operators the referrer has signed up with, similar to redeposit assignment, so it looks like typical deposit behaviour.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and then when they go to create a payout record for bet credit, they then have to piece it out into smaller um, deposit amounts similar to what we do for redeposits. / Joyce Kiddell: typically they would have to chunk it out so that when go to um assign the bet credit to that refer. It like still looks like typical deposit behavior with the operators that those referers have already signed up with.

items.topic: One bulk bet credit payout record
items.statement: Reps send the bet credit as one bulk payment and tell the referrer how to split it across books (usually one book). The payout record logs the total and the per-book split; it is not split into many payout records.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah. Yeah, the rep would typically send 500 and then say, "Okay, 200 on Proline or 250 on Proline, 250 on MGM." If it had to be split up, / Joyce Kiddell: but we don't have to take that payout record itself and make many payout records. It's like just one big bulk one with some like logging on it. / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah.

items.topic: Verify referrer signed up with books
items.statement: Joyce said ideally the system would verify that the referrer is signed up with the specific books before the split is logged.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: they could still like log the total amount and then if we just had fields like we'd have to like verify that that refer is signed up with specific books through the system ideally

items.topic: Book selection with multi-book option
items.statement: Lina suggested indicating the book, with a checkbox for multiple books that opens two or three options.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Okay, if that's one book, then they'll indicate the book and then maybe like a little checklist that's like if multiple books, then you click it and then it drops down to give you two options or three options, you know,

items.topic: Bet credit becomes redeposit records
items.statement: The bet credit payout record is related to redeposit records created by the rep (not ops/BM) and assigned to the referrer's player record. Each follows the normal redeposit process: proof of deposit, then close. All go to the same person.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um Yeah. So Kobi,I think once the the BA kind of does that chunk chunking like within the payout record, we it each uh deposit amount per operator still needs to follow the same flow of like tracking the proof that comes with that deposit. / Kobi Kunasekaran: credit then needs to be related to redeposit records that we create and assign to the player. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and Then that redeposit record then follows the re redeposit process where they have to send proof that they've deposited and then close it off. / Joyce Kiddell: That's right. / Kobi Kunasekaran: okay. So uh the bet credit then effectively like it it does get broken down into redeposit records which in this case are going to be created by the uh by the rep as opposed to like ops or BM in the redeposit conversation we talked about last uh earlier this week. / Joyce Kiddell: Yep.

items.topic: Guided workflow for payout allocation
items.statement: Joyce does not want a clunky process across many screens. Kobi proposed a guided, multi-step workflow: generate the payout, then allocate it into redeposits in the same process. Kobi will come back with the design.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: You know what I mean? Like, we have to really tighten up the workflow if that's the direction we take. / Kobi Kunasekaran: first you generate the redeposit and then click next and it goes to a screen that says okay how do you want to allocate or something like that it could still be part of the same process / Kobi Kunasekaran: We can uh we can potentially like build a guided workflow. So, it's still all part of that same process. But I think I'm just trying to understand like what that process looks like. So, I can come back to you with with that design. / Joyce Kiddell: you you nailed it. that that's correct.
items.critic_note: Firmness kept as decided for the requirement (no clunky multi-screen process; one guided process). Joyce accepted the guided multi-step direction ('Sure.', line 734). The detailed workflow design is still pending from Kobi (item 42).

items.topic: Kobi to design guided payout workflow
items.statement: Kobi will come back with a design for the guided payout-to-redeposit allocation workflow.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We can uh we can potentially like build a guided workflow. So, it's still all part of that same process. But I think I'm just trying to understand like what that process looks like. So, I can come back to you with with that design.

items.topic: Referral payout as redeposit type
items.statement: Joyce suggested adding 'referral payout' as a redeposit type for reporting on overall redeposit budgets. Kobi acknowledged; not explicitly confirmed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: But I feel like having like referral payout as like or refer payout whatever um having that as like a type just in terms of like when we go to like report you know like overall redeposit budgets / Kobi Kunasekaran: Right. Okay. Okay.

items.topic: Same payout creation for cash and bet credit
items.statement: Payout record creation is the same for cash and bet credit. Afterwards, cash conceptually ties to bank transaction(s) (not necessarily required) and bet credit ties to redeposit records. The bet credit payout also captures date sent, BMO ID and currency, with redeposit allocation added on top.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Right. Okay. Okay. So, I think I think I get this out. So, yeah, the the payout record creation is the same for both cash and bad credit. It's just from uh what we do once the payout record is created. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, sorry. um just when the they go to create the record, I think the redeposit version of the payout record is the same in terms of like you still have to capture date the money was sent the BMO ID um and the currency, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. Yeah. Yeah.

items.topic: Secondary referral one-time bonus at 10
items.statement: Secondary referral: a global rule pays a one-time bonus when 10 eligible signups are reached, 200 in redeposit/bet credit or 100 in cash. No further bonuses at 20, 30, etc. Nothing else happens after it is paid.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: um, then you get some sort of bonus. Uh, it's 200 bucks in redeposit or 100 bucks um in cash and it's a onetime thing. So to be clear, that means Lena and Emily that like after the first 10 signups, they're not getting like another bonus at 20 signups and then 30 and 40. Or are they? / Lina Ceniccola: Yes. No. No. 10. They're done. / Kobi Kunasekaran: quies. Okay, this sounds good. Um, so just send for the secondary refer after that's sent out. We're not doing anything else. / Joyce Kiddell: Uh-uh.

items.topic: Secondary paid tracked at referrer level
items.statement: Kobi suggested marking the secondary bonus as paid at the referrer level rather than on the child signups, since it is one-time.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: potentially. Yeah. And I think like we can mark that this has been paid out even at the refer level as opposed to like the child objects because if it's just going to be the one time that might that might make sense.

items.topic: Secondary payout follows primary flows
items.statement: Once the threshold is hit, the secondary payout follows the same flow as primary: cash requires logging that payment was sent and the BMO ID; bet credit follows the bet credit/redeposit path.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, but then to be clear, it's like once they hit that threshold, it then the payout flow begins again. Same as what we just talked about for primary / Joyce Kiddell: follow the same kind of uh bet credit path as the primary

items.topic: Secondary counts all eligible signups
items.statement: Secondary counting ignores the signup's payout type: all eligible (completed) signups count toward 10. The payout type on the secondary payout may default from the referrer, and the rep confirms with the referrer before distributing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: uh everything that's eligible, we just count 10 regardless of the payout type or anything like that on the sign up. And then the moment they get 10, we can create a payout record uh and leave the payout type, maybe do default the payout type based on what's on the referral. And then the rep will then just have to confirm before they distribute it and however which way. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, they would confirm with the the refer.

items.topic: Signups past 10 marked not payable
items.statement: Emily asked whether signups after 10 would carry a status showing they were not paid; Joyce suggested 'not payable'. Not confirmed.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: And then anything after like 10 would have like just a status that indicates it just like wasn't paid out because it's past the something, / Joyce Kiddell: like not applicable or Yeah. / Joyce Kiddell: Not payable.

items.topic: Secondary is discretionary via eligibility flag
items.statement: Instead of always auto-creating a secondary payout at 10 signups (Joyce's ask, Kobi's earlier proposal), secondary payouts are at the rep's discretion. An 'eligible' flag on the referrer account shows eligibility and comes off once paid; the flag prevents auto-creation of the payout, and the rep creates it manually by picking the 10 signups like primary.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: um you could I don't know like um what I'm trying to say is like it doesn't necessarily need to be paid out. It's more if they want to / Emily Vandenberg: I was thinking like a flag at the referer account like just that eligible to and then it would come off like once it's paid out. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I think we can do that. So, we could have a flag on the refer and then that flag could prevent the auto creation of the payout record once the 10 eligible ones are created. Um, but if they do want to go back and like pay the refer then they would do it manually like they just / Kobi Kunasekaran: pick use 10 similar to the primary uh and then pay it out. Yeah, I think we can do that. That could work.

items.topic: Related lists for redeposits and payouts

So like when you're thinking of building out redeposits, you're going to be like bolting them on to the like if you look up player like at a player or like whatever refer you can kind of see all the redeposits and the different statuses that are sitting there for that player. So, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, like uh as long as there's like a lookup field or like we're relating something to another object, generally speaking, yeah, we can create that related list on either or, right?

I'm like feeling like for this phase it's handled after. But what are you thinking? / Joyce Kiddell: Sorry. I was thinking commission already. I was jumping straight to the bottom. items.topic: No separate player payout workflow
items.statement: Player payouts (money sent for signup deposits and redeposits) need no separate workflow or batching; they are one-to-one and tracked on the signup and redeposit records, pulled into reports from the correct fields.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. But so for the player payouts, we don't need to track this separately, right? Uh outside of just on the signup records themselves. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: okay just one to one okay / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. No, no separate workflow required. It's more like just um pulling from the correct fields when we go to surface this in terms of reports

items.topic: Signup has deposit and actual deposit fields
items.statement: Kobi said the signup record already has fields for deposit amount and actual deposit amount; Emily confirmed players sometimes deposit a different amount.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we have that on the signup record now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like we have the option for them to specify the uh a deposit amount and an actual deposit amount.

items.topic: Reports use actual deposit, else expected
items.statement: For payout reporting, pull the actual deposit amount if completed; otherwise default to the deposit amount, for both signups and redeposits.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think when we're going to make the report, Kobe, it would just be like a requirement of um pulling from that field um if it's completed. / Joyce Kiddell: And if it's not, then you can default to the deposit amounts for both signups and redeposits.

items.topic: Do not track money sent to players
items.statement: The system does not track that money was sent to a player for the signup deposit, and no BMO ID is captured for these deposits. Proof, amount and date are captured only when the player reports the deposit; a different actual amount is entered if needed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um we are not we uh my question was we don't need to track that we've sent them this amount in in in the system right now. / Joyce Kiddell: Correct. Yeah, we don't have to capture like um like the Beimo ID or anything as they're sending these deposits. / Joyce Kiddell: It's would be just way too hard to um manage that manually.

items.topic: Payouts scope is referrers only
items.statement: The payouts build covers referrer payments based on the signups they bring in; referral payouts track only referral payments, at the referrer level, not signup payouts or a BA-level/ops view.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Okay, that seems straightforward. Okay, so payouts really is just for referrals uh or referers uh based on the / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, / Kobi Kunasekaran: signups that they're bringing in. / Joyce Kiddell: for sure. Hence why we combine the two flows. / Emily Vandenberg: You're just talking about referral payment payout. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. Yes. That's that's all we're tracking with the payouts here, right?

items.topic: Fraud-flagged signups block payment
items.statement: Signups flagged for fraud before payment must not be paid; signups still in review may be paid later if cleared.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, uh, to be clear, if a refer's signups are flagged for fraud, they should not be paid. Right? Everyone aligned. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, like they if depending on I guess like the confirmed like if it's in review, they might be able to be paid down the road if it turns out they're not, but in a flag status like we shouldn't pay them. / Lina Ceniccola: So, as long as it's flagged beforehand, it should block that payment.

items.topic: Remove signups from batch, cancel payout
items.statement: If a signup or referrer is flagged mid-batch, the rep must be able to take signups out of the batch and cancel or delete the payout. Later limited to unpaid batches.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um you should be able to take signups out of that batch, / Joyce Kiddell: Kobe. Um, and you should be able to cancel um, obviously or delete that same payout.

items.topic: Flagged signups visible but not selectable
items.statement: Signups flagged for fraud (under review, not yet confirmed) stay visible in the payout selection list but cannot be added to a payout; this prompts the rep to check with ops.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, the ones that are like under review or suspected, we still allow them to add them to a payout. / Joyce Kiddell: we I wouldn't allow them to be added to a payout, but have it still be like visible and like you can circle back to it later kind of thing. / Emily Vandenberg: I agree. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. So, they still see it on the list, but they just can't add it to the payout or like when they're creating that payment. / Joyce Kiddell: yes.

items.topic: Confirmed fraud removed from selection list
items.statement: Joyce first wanted confirmed-fraud signups kept in the queue with a visual cue. Kobi raised that they would build up as noise; Emily said they should clear out. Kobi proposed showing confirmed fraud on the referrer record instead of the selection screen, and Joyce accepted as long as it is all visible in the same view (exact meaning of 'same view' not clarified).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: even if it is confirmed as fraud, my gut is leaning towards like keeping it in the queue, but just like not allowing them to add it at all and then have like a big like X or like some sort visual cue / Emily Vandenberg: It should though. It should clear out if it's confirmed, / Kobi Kunasekaran: they would see that on the player record as oppo uh sorry not player but the referral record as opposed to like the screen where they select the batches is what I'm thinking. / Joyce Kiddell: Okay. And that's fine as long as it's all visible in the same view. You know what I mean? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah.

items.topic: Ops report to manage fraud flags
items.statement: Emily wants a report for ops to manage and confirm flagged signups; Kobi said that will be separate from the payout selection.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: definitely want like a report where ops is kind of like managing that to like confirm them. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that'll be separate.

items.topic: Fraud status values: confirmed vs dismissed
items.statement: Kobi described fraud outcomes on signups: 'confirmed' means confirmed fraud (a final status); 'dismissed' removes the fraud flag and reopens the signup, making it eligible. Lina described a 'confirmed success' vs 'confirmed fraud' concept, which caused some confusion.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh in the same way if they have um like anything that's a confirmed fraud um but it never goes out of that queue because confirm fraud is a last status for fraud for a signup. / Lina Ceniccola: There's like a confirmed um flow and then there's kind of there's two layers to it. It's either confirmed like success or confirmed fraud. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Dismissed is would actually just remove the fraud flag. So then it just reopens the signup record.

items.topic: No minimum threshold for primary referrers
items.statement: Primary referrers have no minimum signup threshold before qualifying for payment.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: All right. Is there some sort of minimum thresholds for primary referers before they qualify for commission? / Lina Ceniccola: No.

items.topic: BA commission threshold logic not built
items.statement: A BA commission threshold rule was discussed (details omitted under data-handling rule 5). Joyce and Kobi agreed it is not logic to build now because commissions are not in this phase; it is for reference when reporting is built.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: got it. Yeah. Yeah, I don't know that it's logic we have to build in Kobe, but just for your own reference um when we go to LA build reporting. So, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean, we're not doing commissions right now, / Joyce Kiddell: ignore. / Kobi Kunasekaran: so I don't think this needs to be added in yet.

items.topic: Incomplete redeposits tracked at redeposit level
items.statement: When a bet-credit redeposit cannot complete, it is marked at the redeposit record level (cancel or write off, or cancel if funds come back), and amounts can roll up to the payout for reporting, instead of changing the payout status. The amount does not go back to the pool. Further handling can be added later if needed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: But if um a redeposit does not end the way that we want it to and we get the money back, then we need a status on a payout level / Lina Ceniccola: I would just say have the ability to cancel or like either write it off or if they get the funds back then they can just cancel it. / Kobi Kunasekaran: should we track this at the red deposit level then and then maybe roll up any amounts that was like not completed uh to the payout as opposed to changing the payout status? / Joyce Kiddell: Yes. / Joyce Kiddell: I think it doesn't have to go back to the pool cuz if in the scenario of them going to jail, you're just like not going to continue to pay them. / Kobi Kunasekaran: maybe we'll we'll start with that and then if we do need to add additional layers and complexities around like how to handle the payout with incomplete redeposits, maybe you can come back around to that later.
items.supersedes_hint: Joyce first proposed a new payout-level status (line 1118); the group settled on redeposit-level tracking with roll-up instead.

items.topic: Two incomplete outcomes on redeposits
items.statement: Emily said an incomplete redeposit has two outcomes to track: money lost (erosion / write-off) or funds returned, as two separate incomplete statuses.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: cuz like at the redeposit level it's like it can in be incomplete and there's two things and I know we're not there but like it's going to end up being erosion and a write off because we've lost that money because they didn't send it back but we knew it no it didn't complete. / Emily Vandenberg: So you kind of have to track both or it cannot complete and we get the money back. So there's like a a record that will come back into us, but to be able down the line, right, to pull that, you know, more of the payment flow in, it's just like two separate statuses of incomplete.

items.topic: Paid payout locked; unpaid allows removal
items.statement: Once a payout is marked paid, the record is locked so reps cannot change it; fraud found later is eaten as a write-off. If the payout is not yet paid, reps can remove signups marked as fraud from the batch.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. And like that goes back to what I was saying about if it's already in a batch, then we need the ability to take it out. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But only if the batch isn't already paid. Right. / Joyce Kiddell: Yes. Yeah. If it's already been paid, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. So, once a payout for cash is already marked as paid, / Kobi Kunasekaran: um then we lock that record. So, reps can't do anything with it. But if it's still not marked as paid, then they have the option to remove signups that are marked as flawed from that batch.

items.topic: Signup paid flag split primary/secondary
items.statement: The signup record is marked paid for the referral payout, with primary and secondary referral payments tracked separately; the rep records payment on the payout record.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we're marking the sign up as paid, but paid for like I think we'll separate like uh primary referral payment or and secondary referral payments just so we can keep track of uh both. But yeah, ultimately the signup record will be marked as paid for the referral commission or referral payout. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. Okay.

items.topic: Deal commercial terms do not affect payouts
items.statement: Deal commercial terms are ops-level reporting only and have no impact on referral payouts.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Like we talked about like the uh commercial terms on the deal and stuff. Those are all at the like ops level reporting. Like this has no implication on any like referral payouts or anything like that, right? / Joyce Kiddell: No,

items.topic: Separate financial reporting scoping session
items.statement: Financial reporting (total payouts across everything) needs a separate scoping session. Kobi said reports on existing objects/fields can be added afterwards and create no dependency now. No owner or date was set.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, I think we'll need a separate scoping session on just like reports in general. Um, but that would be the only other piece to this is like the financial reporting like understanding total payouts across everything. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Doesn't need to be it. It doesn't create a dependency at this stage unless you know we have to build something to track

items.topic: Keep rep workflows simple for adoption
items.statement: Emily stressed that the workflows must be simple and logical for reps, who move between logging redeposits and signups, for adoption at launch. Kobi said edge cases and exception handling add complexity; V1 is iterative, the object model is the priority, and UI refinement comes after.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, Kobi.The only thing I'll say is just like keeping in mind like very simple kind of like workflows for and like it really making sense for the reps as they're kind of going through this. / Kobi Kunasekaran: overall like uh we'll we'll try to keep it simple. Um but it's also like an iterative process. So, you know, we V1 doesn't necessarily need to be the final version, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: But the object model is going to be the most important for reporting.

items.topic: Kobi to deliver design documents

Redeposits um and commercial terms as well. So, uh, by mid to end next week is going to be my target. / Joyce Kiddell: mid would be great. Thank you. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'll try it.

items.topic: Two currencies and amounts per signup
items.statement: Each signup carries two currency concepts and two amounts: the currency/amount used to pay the player, and the referrer's payout currency/amount (from the referrer's payment preference and the matrix). The referrer's typical currency (e.g. Ontario vs New Jersey) should feed in automatically so the BA has one less field to choose. Kobi agreed; Emily said it is 'blurry' but accepted, and Kobi will diagram it (see item 33).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: There's two concepts of currencies if I'm correct um with each signup where there's a currency for / Joyce Kiddell: how you pay the player and then there's a currency associated with the the refer / Emily Vandenberg: Okay. Yeah, it's blurry, but it's fine if you guys got it. / Joyce Kiddell: No, it's confusing because we were like talking in terms of currency per sign up, but like there's really two currencies and there's two amounts. / Kobi Kunasekaran: There's two currencies. Yeah.

items.topic: Payout/commission calculation automation deferred
items.statement: Joyce said more automation of player payout and BA commission calculation (e.g. audit trails on bank account activity) is possible but not for now. Kobi agreed: get the data coming out of Salesforce first, then layer in automation later because commission rules change often.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: and there's probably more stuff that we can do to automate like the player and VA commission calculation for like you know audit trails around like bank account activity blah blah blah but like for right now / Kobi Kunasekaran: might be better to make sure we have the data uh coming out of Salesforce first and then we can start layering in bits and pieces to automate that later.

items.topic: Signups leave selection list when batched
items.statement: Kobi described the happy path: once signups are added to a payout record, they are removed from the list of signups eligible for the next batch. This is triggered by adding to a payout, which is earlier than the 'paid' status update in item 34; how this interacts with removing signups from an unpaid batch (item 68) was not explicitly confirmed by the client.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um as I choose signups to be paid out, once they're added to a payout record, uh those signups will be removed from the list of signups that are eligible for the next batch that they create.

items.topic: Payout status gated by completion steps
items.statement: Kobi said the payout status will be driven by completion steps: for cash, required payout details must be filled before the rep can mark it complete; for bet credit, the rep must create the redeposit records in the next step. No explicit client confirmation of the gating rule.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean we decided on like we uh a status right on the payout. So for cash payment before they mark it as complete they should they have to fill out what what type of payout type it is for the bet credit they would have to create the redeposit records in the next step. So I think that will kind of feed into the status.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: External handling of payment matrix The payment matrix is handled outside of Salesforce for the current phase.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Joyce Kiddell: Sorry. I was thinking commission already. I was jumping straight to the bottom. Um yeah, I have a baby so I'm very tired. Um but the uh so what I said apply that to VAcommission. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we're not doing commissions right now. What's that?
gemini_disagreements.why: Misattributed. Joyce corrected herself: the 'handle outside this phase' answer applied to BA commission, not to a payment matrix. The primary referral payment matrix does drive signup payout amounts in Salesforce (Kobi, line 542). Details line 139 repeats the same error.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Handled player payouts outside of Salesforce for the current phase without separate complex workflows.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. But so for the player payouts, we don't need to track this separately, right? Uh outside of just on the signup records themselves. Okay. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. No, no separate workflow required. It's more like just um pulling from the correct fields when we go to surface this in terms of reports
gemini_disagreements.why: Transcript says player payouts need no separate workflow and are tracked on signup/redeposit records in Salesforce for reporting; it does not say they are handled outside Salesforce.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Payment restriction for fraudulent signups Referrers with signups flagged or confirmed for fraud are blocked from receiving payouts.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: So, as long as it's flagged beforehand, it should block that payment. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. So, they still see it on the list, but they just can't add it to the payout or like when they're creating that payment.
gemini_disagreements.why: Overgeneralized. The block applies to the flagged signups (they cannot be added to a payout), not to the referrer as a whole; in-review signups may be paid later if cleared.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: They agreed to keep confirmed fraud signups visible within the record with a clear visual cue so representatives can investigate further before proceeding (01:08:15) (01:12:59). / Implement Fraud Logic: ... Ensure that signups confirmed as fraud remain visible for record keeping but are blocked from batch payments.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they would see that on the player record as oppo uh sorry not player but the referral record as opposed to like the screen where they select the batches is what I'm thinking. / Joyce Kiddell: Okay. And that's fine as long as it's all visible in the same view. You know what I mean?
gemini_disagreements.why: The 'visual cue in the queue' was Joyce's initial position, which was replaced: confirmed fraud signups come out of the batch selection screen and are visible on the referrer record. Gemini blends the flagged (visible, not selectable) and confirmed-fraud rules.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Joyce Kiddell, Emily Vandenberg, Lina Ceniccola] Discuss integrations: Convene offline to determine the best path for integrating Salesforce with third party tools.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Joyce Kiddell: Okay, let me sec cuz Uh yeah, we could just end up using that like after and maybe we like I don't know let's talk about offline in terms of the integration phase tool because it might be faster to go to rippling
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than the transcript and owners are inferred: Joyce only suggested 'let's talk about offline'; no owners were assigned.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The team agreed to set up the November 1 launch so that Salesforce provides the raw data while Jay's tool handles internal commission calculations.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: So Lena, the way I would kind of see that is like an integration with um Jay's tool where now just like the data would be coming from like kind of Salesforce
gemini_disagreements.why: The split of responsibility (data from Salesforce, calculation in Jay's tool) is supported, but how data reaches Jay's tool (integration vs export) was not decided; the summary's framing as an agreed integration is firmer than the transcript. Recorded against the open-question item only.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Concluding the meeting, Kobi Kunasekaran committed to completing and sharing the design documents by mid-to-end of the following week (01:29:24).

gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript: Kobi stated a target and 'I'll try', not a commitment.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: confirming that during Kobi Kunasekaran's upcoming vacation, team members Wy, Taryn Reithofer, and Cedric would step in to cover the build and discovery phases (00:00:12).

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Kobi Kunasekaran] Design Secondary Referral: Develop the secondary referral payout process to trigger after 10 signups. Include an eligibility flag on the referer account to allow for discretionary payout management.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I think we can do that. So, we could have a flag on the refer and then that flag could prevent the auto creation of the payout record once the 10 eligible ones are created. Um, but if they do want to go back and like pay the refer then they would do it manually
